articles.headline: Man United rescue draw at Fulham after own goal shocker
articles.description: A comical own goal by Lisandro Martinez saw Manchester United fail to win for a third Premier League game in a row as they drew 1-1 with Fulham at Craven Cottage.
articles.body:
A comical own goal by Lisandro Martínez saw Manchester United fail to win for a third Premier League game in a row as they drew 1-1 with Fulham at Craven Cottage.

It was a lethargic, muted display from Michael Carrick's side, who will spend the international break in the bottom half of the Premier League table, though they were spared from making it three losses in a week by Matheus Cunha's late deflected goal.

Their malaise was summed up by the surreal nature of the goal they gifted Fulham.

It went down against Martinez's name but the blame was shared with his goalkeeper, a botched effort by Senne Lammens to shovel away Calvin Bassey's shot with his legs rather than his gloves, then an equally inexplicable and muddled attempt at keeping the defender's pass back to him out of his net.

Cunha too had been at fault, crumpling into a heap in midfield and allowing Bassey to sprint the ball away, though the Brazilian would redeem himself, rescuing his side in the 89th minute with a shot that deflected heavily off David Affengruber.

There could be little arguing United deserved anything more than they got, indeed Fulham ought to have given Alvaro Arbeloa his first Premier League win.

There was plenty here to offer the Spaniard encouragement. Early on, Antonee Robinson moved the ball inside to Gonzalo García who shot wide in search of his second Premier League goal. Martinez hit a thunderous effort from range that needed turning away at full-stretch by Bernd Leno.

The game had been played at a sedentary, almost pre-season pace but burst suddenly into life midway through the half.

United came within inches of going ahead when Cunha got the better of Affengruber near the byline and cut back for Bruno Fernandes to roll a shot against a post.

Lammens, prior to his second-half howler, made three saves in quick succession, the best of them a smart block from Sander Berge. Oscar Bobb then dragged wide from a good position before Leno was needed again to tip away Cunha's awkward deflected effort.

The United goalkeeper had a perplexing afternoon. At times he was keeping his team in it, sticking out a boot to divert Josh King's low shot behind, then later racing from goal to smother as Alex Iwobi went through.

A lovely turn and cross by Cunha found Marcus Rashford, arguably still not looking at ease back at United, who leaned back and leathered his effort into the Fulham supporters behind the goal.

United got themselves into a horrible mess for Fulham's goal. Cunha made a feeble attempt to keep the ball from Bassey, who put the Brazilian on the floor and raced into the box. His shot was tame and straight at Lammens who made the strange decision to bounce away with his thigh, then could not recover as Martinez's pass back to him squirmed into the corner.

Bryan Mbeumo was denied by a flying save from Leno, who also kept out Cunha's curling effort as it bent towards the bottom corner.

articles.headline: Phillies option Orion Kerkering to Triple-A, call up Max Lazar
articles.description: The Phillies optioned reliever Orion Kerkering to Triple-A Lehigh Valley after he posted an 18.69 ERA in his four appearances this month.
articles.body:
NEW YORK -- The Philadelphia Phillies optioned reliever Orion Kerkering to Triple-A Lehigh Valley on Sunday after he posted an 18.69 ERA in his four appearances this month.

The right-hander gave up four runs in the eighth inning of Saturday's 10-3 loss to the New York Mets, after which interim manager Don Mattingly admitted he was concerned about the 25-year-old and uncertain where he could continue using him.

"You have to be able to use him there in a game like that," Mattingly said. "Not going to try to chase a three-run deficit in that inning. It's hard to find places to use him."

Kerkering established himself as one of the Phillies' most reliable setup men by going 13-7 with a 2.78 ERA and four saves over the previous two seasons. But he committed a season-ending throwing error in the 11th inning of Game 4 of the 2025 National League Division Series, when he tossed the ball over the head of catcher J.T. Realmuto trying to force out Hyeseong Kim, who scored the winning run in the Los Angeles Dodgers' 2-1 victory.

Kerkering opened this season with a 2.03 ERA in his first 29 appearances and still had an ERA below 3.00 through July 28. He is 1-1 with a 10.80 ERA and one save in his last 19 appearances.

To replace Kerkering on the active roster, the Phillies promoted right-hander Max Lazar from Lehigh Valley.

articles.headline: Packers WR Reed, RT Bako-Bewele carted off with injuries
articles.description: Packers wide receiver Jayden Reed and right tackle Zach Bako-Bewele were carted off the field on back-to-back plays Sunday.
articles.body:
EAST RUTHERFORD, N.J. - Green Bay Packers receiver Jayden Reed was carted off the field after being placed on a stabilizing backboard following the second play from scrimmage in Sunday's game against the New York Jets at MetLife Stadium.

On the very next play, Packers right tackle Zach Bako-Bewele sustained a right leg injury and also was carted off the field. Bako-Bewele's leg was immediately placed in a cast before he got on the cart.

Both players were quickly ruled out for the game by the Packers.

Members of the medical staff from both teams attended to Reed for several minutes on the field before he was placed on a board and had his helmet strapped down for stabilization.

Reed took what appeared to be a hit in the head and neck area at the end of a 4-yard gain on a swing pass in the left flat. Jets linebacker Demario Davis was the initial defender to hit Reed, and then Kingsley Enagbare also may have made contact with Reed after that.

Players from both teams took a knee while Reed was down.

The weekend of soccer across Europe continues!

In the Premier League, Manchester City will spend the international break three points clear of champions Arsenal at the top of the table after a thrilling 5-3 win over Sunderland on Sunday. Meanwhile Liverpool boss Andoni Iraola got a 1-0 win on his return to former club Bournemouth. 

Later, Manchester United managed to come back late to draw Fulham 1-1 in a result that was not the bounce-back they wanted after losing the derby and getting eliminated midweek in the Carabao Cup.

In LaLiga, Atlético Madrid beat Real Madrid, 2-1, in the first Madrid derby of the season. In the Bundesliga, Bayer Leverkusen beat RB Leipzig 2-0. To finish the day in Ligue 1, Marseille will host Paris Saint-Germain in Le Classique.

articles.headline: Enzo Maresca relieved as Manchester City pass difficult Sunderland test
articles.description: Enzo Maresca can enjoy a little relaxation over the international break after Manchester City extended their perfect start to the season -- but Sunday's frantic 5-3 win over Sunderland was not good for his blood pressure.
articles.body:
Enzo Maresca can enjoy a little relaxation over the international break after Manchester City extended their perfect start to the season -- but Sunday's frantic 5-3 win over Sunderland was not good for his blood pressure.

Sunderland twice drew level in a chaotic first half, with Brian Brobbey cancelling out goals from Enzo Fernández and Rayan Cherki before Antoine Semenyo put City 3-2 up at the break.

Semenyo extended City's lead further but Brobbey quickly completed his hat trick, and City needed Erling Haaland's 81st-minute strike to be sure of going three points clear at the top of the Premier League.

Amid the chaos, Sunderland had a penalty shout turned down after Elliot Anderson appeared to handle in the box with the score at 3-2.

"To be honest, I prefer to win 1-0 than 5-3, but I expected a very difficult game," Maresca said. "I knew how they good are, off the ball very aggressive and on the ball they have different weapons, set-pieces, and Brobbey."

Since losing the Community Shield against Arsenal, City have won five straight in the league, also winning their opening Champions League match and beating Norwich in the Carabao Cup.

"I know it was a difficult game, but happy because we found a way to win the game and the good thing also is that these seven official games we played they are all different," Maresca added.

"We experienced different things, the last one with 10 men [against Manchester United], today was a complicated one, the Bournemouth one we were losing 1-0 so also a chance to learn from the game."

Sunderland caused City plenty of problems, not content to sit back and defend but playing on the front foot and denying City the control they usually enjoy at home.

Maresca admitted at least two of the visitors' three goals were "too easy" from a City point of view.

"For sure you can control it better, keeping the ball, but there are games you want to control or keep the ball but there is also another team," Maresca said. "Sunderland-Arsenal last week was another crazy game. There is another team that do their best."

Brobbey's first goals of the season came in a bundle as the 24-year-old became only the sixth player in Premier League history to score a hat trick and finish on the losing side.

"We were not concerned because he didn't score in the first four games," Regis Le Bris said. "He showed so many good signs in training sessions and his mentality on the pitch in the Premier League and Europa League.

"It was just a question of time, and the connection with his teammates is getting better. I'm really pleased for him because it's never easy to have a long period without scoring. Now it's done."

Sunderland ended defeated, but could leave the Etihad with their heads held high after causing City so many problems.

"It's a defeat, but we are proud of the level of the squad," Le Bris added. "We created many chances. Probably deserved to score two or three more goals so it was really tight.

articles.headline: Who is Commanders' special teams ace Tyler Owens?
articles.description: J.J. Watt called Owens' play against the Eagles 'legitimately one of the greatest football plays I've ever seen.'
articles.body:
ASHBURN, Va. -- The play, viewed more than 18 million times on one social media platform, went like this: Washington Commanders special-teamer Tyler Owens, ready to cover a punt, stepped outside then cut back inside and ripped through a double-team at the line of scrimmage. He flung one blocker to the side then stiff-armed the other as he raced downfield. When the other blocker caught back up to Owens, he shoved him to the ground then did the same to the second one.

Owens looked like a man chasing someone stealing his car.

And then Owens reached the returner, who decided to leap. Bad decision. Owens corralled him and body-slammed him to the ground. Owens then got up and casually walked to the sideline, as if he had just clocked out of work for the day.

"It was just a good rep," he said.

Others begged to differ. Former Pro Bowl defensive end J.J. Watt called it "legitimately one of the greatest football plays I've ever seen." It has been viewed more than 11.6 million times on the NFL's X feed and another 6.9 million times on the NFLmemes feed. More than 40,000 people liked it on the NFL's Instagram page.

"I was just out there playing football," Owens said. "It never really stood out to me until after."

And though it introduced Owens to the sporting world, his teammates needed no introductions. They already knew what he could do -- and has done. They might have been impressed by the play, but they were not surprised.

There's a reason Owens made the Commanders as an undrafted free agent in 2024; he made two plays that summer to stand out. Those plays also prompted coach Dan Quinn to make an unusual announcement in a team meeting about Owens. His special teams coach at Texas Tech, Kenny Perry, could point to plays in college that prompted him to tell Owens he would make a long living in the NFL.

"That's what he's been doing," said Washington safety Jeremy Reaves, a special teams Pro Bowler after the 2022 season. "He's done that over and over and over again. That's who he is."

Commanders punter Tress Way, who has been in the league since 2014, said he gets the same question from coordinators or assistant coaches on other teams.

"Just about every team we play, they're like, 'What do you guys feed 18?'" Way said. "I tell them punt returners."

Three days after the play, after he had become a teaching tool for special teams coaches at every level and after seeing the reaction and appearing on "The Pat McAfee Show," Owens knows it was more than "just a good rep."

And though other plays stand out in his mind, this one vs. the Eagles vaulted to the top.

"I would say this is my favorite," Owens said. "Just because of the physicality. ... It's just rewarding. You put in all this work, finally get to see something come out of it."

What he saw was a viral reaction.

"Just all the GOATS retweeting it and stuff like that. It's pretty dope," Owens said. "I like it."

articles.headline: Reds place ace Chase Burns on 15-day IL with groin strain
articles.description: The Reds have placed right-hander Chase Burns on the 15-day injured list with a right groin strain. A first-time All-Star this season, the 23-year-old went 15-3 with a 2.86 ERA.
articles.body:
CINCINNATI -- The Reds placed right-hander Chase Burns on the 15-day injured list Sunday with a right groin strain, ending the All-Star's season.

"After his start [Friday], he just came in ... and he felt the right groin a little bit," Reds manager Terry Francona said. "So again, we're being very cautious."

The move to the IL was retroactive to Saturday.

Burns, 23, has pitched 154⅓ innings this season, far surpassing his 43⅓ innings during his rookie season in 2025. He is 15-3 with a 2.86 ERA, 185 strikeouts and a 1.166 WHIP in 29 starts.

His 238 strikeouts through his first 36 career starts rank third in Reds franchise history since 1900.

Burns had worked three innings in each of his past three starts to limit his innings for the remainder of the season.

"He did a really, really good job," Francona said. "I think it makes sense to not push him for [another] three-inning start. We got him to a point where next year, however he pitches, it's not going to be determined by, 'Oh, we've got to be careful with this.' So that's a really good thing."

Burns was named to the National League All-Star squad but did not pitch because of a groin issue.

"Not how I wanted it to end," Burns said. "Both groins kind of got upset this year. Kind of frustrating. Happy with the way the season went, just the growth and experience. Ready to get back next year. I'm excited."

In corresponding roster moves Sunday, the Reds selected right-hander Carson Spiers from Triple-A Louisville and designated outfielder TJ Friedl for assignment.

Friedl batted .172 with four homers and 13 RBIs in 91 games. He was optioned to Louisville on Friday for the second time this season.

articles.headline: Aaron Rodgers' 2026 NFL season: Tracking records, milestones
articles.description: The Steelers QB, who is entering his 22nd season in the league, is chasing records, and ESPN will be chronicling his "last rodeo."
articles.body:
Entering his 22nd NFL season -- or as Aaron Rodgers says, "his last rodeo" -- the 42-year-old Pittsburgh Steelers quarterback is on the cusp of joining several exclusive clubs as he moves up the ranks in the league record books.

In 2025, he passed former teammate Brett Favre to take sole possession of fourth place in career touchdown passes thrown with his 509th TD pass in the Week 3 win against the New England Patriots.

"Every now and then I made some special throws that led to touchdowns, but I've been playing a long time, and it's a longevity thing," Rodgers said before passing Favre's mark last season. "I'm proud of it, but not a big deal."

Rodgers also went on to supplant Ben Roethlisberger for fifth in all-time passing yards in the second quarter of the Thursday night loss to the Cincinnati Bengals on Oct. 16, 2025.

That Rodgers is still chasing records in 2026 is somewhat of a surprise after he suggested at times during the 2025 season that he was nearing the end of his career.

"It's the twilight of my career," he said after beating the Minnesota Vikings in Ireland on Oct. 5, 2025. "I used to say five, six, seven years ago, I was on the back nine. But I'm teeing off on 18 right now."

In that win, Rodgers made two more noteworthy entries into the record books: most completions of 50-plus yards and second quarterback in NFL history to throw 60 or more touchdown passes against multiple franchises.

But now, Rodgers is closing in on his final opportunities to add to that ever-growing list of historic accomplishments.

Maybe it took him a couple of shots to reach the green, or maybe he took his time finding his shot on the fairway. Either way, the 18th hole is in sight, and Rodgers is crouched in front of his ball, squaring up the putt.

"I thought last year might be it," Rodgers said on the first day of training camp. "And then Mike [McCarthy] got hired. And I talked to the wife, and she said you can do one more year. I said, 'We'll see if it works out.' And it kind of all came together."

Among the milestones in reach for Rodgers are becoming the fourth quarterback in NFL history to appear in 300 games (as of Week 1 he has appeared in 288), joining Tom Brady (383), Favre (326) and Drew Brees (305), throwing the third-most touchdown passes in NFL history (as of Week 1, he has 232) and having the second-most regular-season games with multiple touchdown passes (he only threw for 1 in Week 1). And after Week 1, he needs 3,505 yards to become the fifth player to reach 70,000 passing yards. 

This season, we're chronicling Rodgers' individual milestones week by week as he rides his last rodeo and lines up his putt on the 18th green. Follow along here for the weekly installments.
